description:
GreenDelta states a water use factor for water emitted to water per kilogram -- 0.00698 for France -- and this list publishes that flow per cubic metre. A kilogram of water is a thousandth of a cubic metre, and the build already held that number: BAFU's own kilogram water rows were merged onto the same flows carrying 0.001 m3/kg. The factor pass never looked there. It compared the two unit names, reported a unit crossing and published nothing, 213 times.

**A conversion is a statement about a pair, and the pair is what is keyed.** `matching.recorded_conversions` indexes every multiplier the merge wrote by `(flow, source unit, target unit)`, and a row uses one only where the flow is the same flow and both units are the same units. A kilogram of standing wood is 0.00204 cubic metres and a kilogram of water is 0.001; neither flow is the other. Where one flow carries two values for one pair -- natural gas at 34.5 and 36.0 MJ per cubic metre -- the pair is left out and the rows keep the crossing they had.

**It is a fallback and never an override.** A row that arrives with its own identifier carries the merge's answer for that row, which is unchanged. This is for the rows reached by a name or by a curated decision, which have none.

Measured by running `characterise` twice over the build of 2026-08-29 (`20260829T1149`): 213 factors converted over 5 flows, 211 more published, and `Water` in Environmental → Water → Unknown gains GreenDelta's 209 country factors. Three crossings remain and should: `Water` emitted to a river and `Waste water`, whose flows carry no kilogram conversion of their own, and `Gas, mine, off-gas, process, coal mining`, whose pair has two answers.

**What the 209 show is a disagreement, not an agreement.** GreenDelta states +6.98 for France where the JRC states -6.98, and so for all 209: their package drops the sign on the water-return half of EF's water use pair. `difference_incomparable` rises from 12 to 221 because of it. That is the comparison working -- a difference that was invisible while the factors were being dropped over a unit spelling.

**Re-read from the 2.8.2 package, 2026-10-20 (#386).** The package states its water returns per cubic metre, so the 213 conversions above are no longer needed and the mechanism answers for five factors instead; the three crossings are ten, every one a real change of quantity; and the incomparable count is 17, none of it water. Each claim's comment lists what its number is made of, on the default five-list build of 20 October 2026 (pipeline `20261020T1746012906270000`, merge run `be0df0cc`, characterise run `8467b7b5`, commit a607b4f).

expectations.title: Five flows are published on a conversion the build already recorded
expectations.comment: Counted separately from the factors, because "the build had this number" is a different claim from "this row carried it", and a reader deciding whether to trust a converted factor needs to know which one it was.

expectations.title: Five factors are converted by a conversion the merge recorded rather than dropped
expectations.comment: Restated 2026-10-20 (#386) for the 2.8.2 package, which states `Water` emitted to water per cubic metre itself, so the 209 country factors this change converted from kilograms arrive in the published unit and need no conversion. On the default five-list build of 20 October 2026 (pipeline `20261020T1746012906270000`, merge run `be0df0cc`, characterise run `8467b7b5`, commit a607b4f) the factors GreenDelta publishes in a unit other than the row's are `Water, process, surface` per kilogram onto surface water per cubic metre, `Coal, Hard`, `Coal, Brown`, `Oil, Crude` and `Uranium` per kilogram onto flows published per megajoule, `Gas, Natural` per cubic metre onto natural gas per megajoule, and the coal-mine off-gas per cubic metre onto its flow per standard cubic metre; five of them by a multiplier a merged list recorded for that flow and that pair of units, which is what this counts. 213 was the copy's number.

expectations.title: The ten crossings this build cannot answer are still reported
expectations.comment:
An equality, because the fix must not work by silencing the guard. Restated 2026-10-20 (#386) for the 2.8.2 package, on the default five-list build of 20 October 2026 (pipeline `20261020T1746012906270000`, merge run `be0df0cc`, characterise run `8467b7b5`, commit a607b4f): three before, ten now -- `Water` emitted to a river and to surface water, stated per kilogram against flows published per cubic metre; `Waste Water` to water, unspecified, the same way; `Uranium, 451 GJ Per Kg`, `Uranium, 560 GJ Per Kg`, `Uranium, 2291 GJ Per Kg, In Ground` and `Gas, Natural, 46.8 MJ Per Kg`, stated per kilogram against flows published per megajoule, where the number in the name is not a conversion this list has recorded; and `Gas, Natural/m3` and both `Gas, Mine, Off-gas, Process, Coal Mining` rows, per kilogram and per cubic metre, against flows published per megajoule, where the pair has two recorded answers.

Growing means a route stopped finding a conversion it used to have; shrinking means one of the ten was answered somewhere, which is a reason to re-read this file rather than to let it lapse.

expectations.title: GreenDelta characterises `Water` emitted to water for no place
expectations.comment:
The flow the whole issue is about. Before this change GreenDelta published nothing on it, because their factor is stated per kilogram; the JRC's 209 and the consensus's were there alone.

The magnitudes are the JRC's exactly -- 23.1 for Albania, 6.98 for France -- and the signs are not: theirs are positive where the JRC's are negative, on all 209.

**Restated 2026-10-14.** GreenDelta's factors stated per place are refused for now (#386), so what is left is the one factor their package states for no place: -42.95 per m3; 2.8.2 also states it per kilogram, -0.04295, which is the same number converted, and `lcia.collisions` keeps it once. Restated from the package, and not yet measured on a build. Measured on the build of 20 October 2026, the first with openLCA LCIA methods 2.8.2 merged and characterised (merge run 76b3ec8f): met.

expectations.title: GreenDelta's water factors are comparable with the JRC's; 17 other pairs are not
expectations.comment:
**Rewritten by #172, keeping its id so the baseline keeps this question's history.** It read `at_least: 221`, and said that 209 water factors were reported as incomparable with the JRC's -- 12 before #170 and 221 after, because publishing GreenDelta's country factors on `Water` in `Environmental → Water → Unknown` made a sign disagreement visible that had been hidden while the numbers were being dropped over a unit spelling. That was right about the build and wrong about what to want: #172 applies the sign where the package is read, and the water pair agrees with the JRC's to the digit.

Restated 2026-10-20 (#386) for the 2.8.2 package, on the default five-list build of 20 October 2026 (pipeline `20261020T1746012906270000`, merge run `be0df0cc`, characterise run `8467b7b5`, commit a607b4f): 17, none of them water. Sixteen are a factor the JRC states as exactly zero and GreenDelta as a number, which a ratio cannot express -- 1,1,1-trichloroethane to air in three compartments, chlorobenzene to long-term water, chromium(3+) to non-agricultural soil and aluminium(3+) to long-term air, each once in a toxicity category and once in its organics or inorganics half. The seventeenth is the land-use sign on `Permanent cropland, non-irrigated, extensive`, where the JRC and ecoinvent state +46.211 and GreenDelta −462.11. 12 on the build before the package switch.
